records.question: According to the section, what is the total economic value per year of coral reefs in American Samoa when including resident and visitor nonuse values?
ground_truth_chunks: A study of the economic value of coral reefs and mangroves in American Samoa found that coral reefs had recreational benefits of \$73,000 per year, fisheries benefits of \$759,000, coastal protection benefits of \$447,000 a year, and a total economic value which includes resident and visitor nonuse values, of \$5.1 million a year.

When potential nonuse benefits accruing to the US general public are included, the overall benefits could be in the order of at least US\$10 million/year for coral reefs and US\$1.5 million/year for mangroves.

records.question: What factors make logging unprofitable in American Samoa?
records.ground_truth_answer: Most native trees are too small and not straight enough to be commercially valuable; the slopes are too steep to log; and the islands are too small and remote for logging to be profitable.
ground_truth_chunks: In American Samoa, most of the native trees are too small and not straight enough to be commercially valuable, the slopes too steep to log, and islands too small and remote for logging to be profitable.
The slopes are also too steep for coconut groves, so most of the territory retains uncut forest, which holds water and soil from runoff.

records.question: What regulations or actions does section 28.13 suggest have been among the most helpful for maintaining reef health in American Samoa?
records.ground_truth_answer: Banning scuba spearfishing and culling of crown-of-thorns starfish.
ground_truth_chunks: Large reef fish species are overfished, reef flats have been dredged or built on, and crown-ofthorns starfish outbreaks have killed large amounts of coral.
Perhaps, the banning of scuba spearfishing and culling of crown-of-thorns starfish have been among the most helpful regulations and actions.
